notes.body: The Japanese here says bōya, literally ‘boy.’ At the time it was also used as an affectionate way to address any small child, even the little girl described earlier.
The baby’s sound echoes the Japanese word umai, meaning tasty or yummy. The English keeps it as babble rather than turning it into words.

data.say: Kept two Curious notes on what English cannot carry, bōya and uma-uma, and left vessels, vision and counts to the text itself.
